text: Suddenly there came into view a decrepit old man of some sixty five or seventy years, whose countenance at once arrested and absorbed my whole attention, on account of its absolute strangeness. <break time="0.8s" /> Never before had I seen anything even remotely resembling that expression, and as I tried to analyze it, a crowd of contradictory ideas arose confusedly in my mind. <break time="0.8s" /> Ideas of vast mental power, of caution and avarice, of coolness and malice, of triumph and merriment, of excessive terror, and of intense, supreme despair all seemed written upon that single face. <break time="0.8s" /> How wild a history, I said to myself, is written within that bosom, and I felt a craving desire to keep the man in view, to know more of him. <break time="0.8s" /> Hurriedly putting on my overcoat and seizing my hat and cane, I made my way into the street and pushed through the crowd in the direction he had taken, for he had already disappeared. <break time="0.8s" /> With some little difficulty I at length came within sight of him, and I followed closely yet cautiously, so as not to attract the attention of this strange and restless figure. <break time="0.8s" /> He was short in stature, very thin, and apparently very feeble, and his clothes were filthy and ragged, yet the linen he wore, though dirty, was of beautiful texture. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a rent in his closely buttoned cloak, I caught a glimpse both of a diamond and of a dagger, a discovery which only heightened my curiosity and made me resolve to follow him wherever he went.
